# Results — Study 267 (M2-Growth) on M2 YoY × ^GSPC monthly

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). M2 YoY growth is
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../m2_growth/data.py) (monthly anchors, FRED M2SL
contour, 1960–2025) and joined to ^GSPC monthly price returns (yfinance,
cache-only at `_cache/gspc_monthly.parquet`). Match the fingerprint below to
confirm you hold the same ^GSPC tape. As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC monthly close (price only, yfinance) | 1985-01 – 2025-12 | 492 months | `ecbbebebec4e` |
| M2 YoY growth (hardcoded, FRED M2SL contour) | 1960-01 – 2025-12 | monthly | hardcoded constant |
| Merged panel (inner join, 1-mo lag) | 1985-01 – 2025-12 | 491 usable months | — |

> **No look-ahead.** The M2 reading dated month *t* (itself released weeks late)
> predicts the ^GSPC return earned in month *t+1* (`sp_fwd1`) and over the next
> 12 months (`sp_fwd12`). Returns are **price only** (no dividends).

## Predictive regression — lagged M2 YoY → forward ^GSPC return

| Horizon | β (per +1pp M2) | t (OLS, naive) | **t (HAC, honest)** | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Next 1 month  | ≈ 0.0000  | −0.01 | **−0.01** | 0.000 |
| Next 12 months (overlapping) | −0.0033 | **−2.01** | **−0.57** | 0.008 |

- The **1-month** forward regression is a non-event: β ≈ 0, HAC t ≈ −0.01.
- The **12-month** regression is the teaching moment. The naive OLS t is −2.01
  and *looks* significant — but the windows overlap, inflating the t. The
  Newey-West (HAC, 18-lag) t collapses to **−0.57**. Whatever signal seems to be
  there is an artifact of overlapping-window autocorrelation.
- Note the **sign is negative**: if anything, faster money growth precedes
  *weaker* forward returns — the opposite of the bullish folk claim.

## Quantile sort — high-money vs low-money months (next-month return)

| Bucket (lagged M2 YoY) | mean next-month ^GSPC return |
|---|--:|
| Lowest M2 growth | **+1.28%** |
| Highest M2 growth | **+0.06%** |
| **High − Low spread** | **−1.22pp** (Welch t = **−1.87**) |

The high-money bucket *underperforms* the low-money bucket by 1.2pp/month, with
a t-stat that does not clear |2|. The chart-overlay intuition (more money ⇒
higher returns) is contradicted in both sign and significance.

## Tradable rule — long ^GSPC when lagged M2 YoY > trailing 60-mo median, else cash

| Metric | M2 rule (net) | Buy & hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| Annualized return | **+2.81%** | **+9.31%** |
| Sharpe | **0.32** | **0.67** |
| Time in market | 39.7% | 100% |
| Turnover (flips/yr) | 0.27 | — |

One-way cost = 5 bps on NAV per flip (long/flat ⇒ no borrow). The rule is in the
market only 40% of the time and gives up two-thirds of the equity return. Costs
are negligible (turnover is tiny) — the failure is the *signal*, not the friction.

## Positive control (synthetic)

With the engine pointed at a synthetic panel where a known M2 premium is planted
into next-month returns, the HAC t scales cleanly with the planted size
(premium 0.0 → t ≈ 0.3; 0.5 → t ≈ 6; 1.0 → t ≈ 12; 2.0 → t ≈ 24). The machinery
detects a real link when one exists. The real tape has none.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Lagged M2 YoY has no robust predictive content for forward
  ^GSPC returns: 1-month HAC t ≈ 0.0; 12-month HAC t ≈ −0.6 (the naive −2.0
  evaporates under the overlap correction); the high-minus-low monthly spread is
  *negative* and insignificant. No HAC t clears the |t| ≥ 2 bar — and the sign is
  wrong for the bullish claim. *(Caveat: price-only ^GSPC and a survivorship-free
  single index, but a richer tape would not rescue a near-zero, wrong-signed t.)*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long/flat M2 rule earns +2.8%/yr net vs +9.3%/yr
  for passive buy-and-hold, at half the Sharpe, sitting out 60% of the time.
  There is no edge to harvest.
- **The overlay deceives because it is contemporaneous.** Money and markets both
  surge when the Fed eases into a downturn; once you lag the (already-lagged) M2
  release and demand a HAC t-stat, the "money drives stocks" story does not pay.
